semantic.how_to_run: Install the ml extra (pip install -e ".[dev,ml]", with the CPU-only PyTorch first on Linux as the README shows), then run python -m evals.run --semantic. The first run downloads the two models from Hugging Face, about 180 MB.

llm.how_to_run: Put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment or in a local .env file (see the README), then run python -m evals.run --llm. It makes one parse call per job and up to LLM_MAX_SUGGESTIONS rewrite candidates per pair (20 by default).

error_analysis.title: Requirements that name no catalog skill are left for a person to check
error_analysis.observation: The rule parser only finds skills from the skill catalog. A requirement whose tools are outside it, or that asks for a domain, a degree or a certification, gets no skills, so exact matching marks it needs_check whether the resume proves it, lacks it or shows it in part.

examples.what: "Experience with RxJS and NgRx": labeled partial; the parser found no catalog skill in it.
"Experience with Next.js or another server-side rendering framework is required.": labeled direct; the parser found no catalog skill in it.
"Solid understanding of statistics and model evaluation": labeled direct; the parser found no catalog skill in it.

error_analysis.title: Years requirements cite no resume lines
error_analysis.observation: For a years-only requirement the report gives the years it counted but no lines, while the labels cite the role header lines. These items always miss in evidence recall, which is why recall is also shown without them.

examples.what: "5+ years of professional software or data engineering experience": labeled direct; the report cites no lines (8.9 years read).
"5+ years of professional software or data engineering experience": labeled direct; the report cites no lines (13.3 years read).
"5+ years of professional software or data engineering experience": labeled direct; the report cites no lines (no years read).

error_analysis.title: Required lines get the wrong priority
error_analysis.observation: Required lines written as prose sentences, or under a heading the parser doesn't know, default to context; a line-level word such as "Familiarity with" turns a required line into preferred.

examples.what: "Familiarity with Git and CI/CD workflows" labeled required, parsed as preferred.
"We are looking for someone with 4+ years of professional front-end development experience." labeled required, parsed as context.
"Experience with PyTorch or TensorFlow" labeled required, parsed as context.

error_analysis.title: Benefits, pay and legal lines after an unknown heading are kept as requirements
error_analysis.observation: A heading the parser doesn't know ("What we offer") doesn't end the section above it, so benefit, salary, equal opportunity and how-to-apply lines are kept with that section's priority.

examples.what: "Salary range: $150,000 - $175,000 plus annual bonus" kept as preferred.
"Compensation: $160,000 - $190,000 base, plus equity." kept as preferred.
"Excellent compensation and benefits. Example Coastal Insurance is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Please sha..." kept as preferred.

error_analysis.title: Related experience needs matching by meaning
error_analysis.observation: In exact mode the app never returns adjacent, so related experience the labels mark adjacent (GitLab CI for GitHub Actions, Java for C#) comes out as gap, partial or needs_check. Matching by meaning is meant for these and wasn't run.

examples.what: "Experience with GitHub Actions": labeled adjacent, app gap (GitHub Actions missing, Git missing).
"Experience with GitHub Actions": labeled adjacent, app partial (GitHub Actions missing, Git demonstrated).
"Knowledge of Guidewire or other insurance platforms": labeled adjacent, app partial (Guidewire missing, Insurance listed).

error_analysis.title: The status is right but the first lines cited aren't the labeled ones
error_analysis.observation: The status matches the label, but none of the report's first three lines is a labeled evidence line. Evidence is listed skill by skill, so the first lines can all come from one skill of the requirement, or from a broad skill such as ETL (matched by "data pipelines").

examples.what: "Experience building data pipelines on AWS or Azure": labeled direct, app direct; first line: experience line "Implemented CI/CD for data pipelines with Azure DevOps." (ETL via 'data pipelines').
"Healthcare or insurance data experience": labeled direct, app direct; first line: experience line "Data Scientist - Demo Insurance Group - May 2019 to Jul 2021" (Insurance via 'Insurance').

"Guidewire certification (Associate or Specialist)": labeled direct, app direct; first line: experience line "Senior Guidewire Developer, Example Mutual, Jacksonville, FL | Apr 2022 - Till date" (Guidewire via 'Guidewire').

error_analysis.title: Years requirements fail when roles weren't read
error_analysis.observation: A years requirement is decided from the roles the app read: their total for "5+ years of experience", and the roles that mention the skill for "4+ years with Java". When a role is lost (see the structure patterns) the years fall short and the requirement becomes a gap or partial, or needs_check when no role was read at all.

examples.what: "5+ years of professional software or data engineering experience": labeled direct, app needs_check with no years read in total.
"5+ years of experience in software engineering, DevOps or systems administration": labeled direct, app needs_check with no years read in total.
"5+ years of backend software development experience": labeled direct, app gap with 1.3 years read in total.

error_analysis.title: Work the labels count as shown is found only in a summary or skills line
error_analysis.observation: The labels count the work as shown in a bullet, but the bullet describes it in other words, so exact matching finds the skill only in the summary or skills section, or not at all, and calls the requirement partial.

examples.what: "Background in the insurance industry": labeled direct, app partial (Insurance listed).
"Familiarity with Git and CI/CD workflows": labeled direct, app partial (Git demonstrated, CI/CD missing).
"Hands-on NLP experience, including transformer models": labeled direct, app partial (NLP listed).

error_analysis.title: A resume without section headings yields no roles or education
error_analysis.observation: Roles are read only from an experience section and education only from an education section. With no headings every line is in the header section, so no role, date, total years or degree is read.

examples.what: role 'Backend Developer, Sample Retail Group': The line is in the header section, and roles are only read from an experience section. Extracted line: "Backend Developer, Sample Retail Group | Feb 2023 - Present".

role 'Python Developer, Demo Startup Labs': The line is in the header section, and roles are only read from an experience section. Extracted line: "Python Developer, Demo Startup Labs | Apr 2020 - Jan 2023".

role 'Junior Developer, Placeholder Web Studio': The line is in the header section, and roles are only read from an experience section. Extracted line: "Junior Developer, Placeholder Web Studio | Jul 2019 - Mar 2020".

error_analysis.title: Company and posting details are kept as requirements
error_analysis.observation: Company descriptions and posting lines (company, client) are kept as context requirements: before the first heading when they name a catalog skill (a company name with "Insurance" in it), and inside a role section as one more sentence.

examples.what: "Company: Sample Insurance Holdings" kept as context.
"Demo Freight Systems is growing the team that runs our order and shipment platform." kept as context.
"Client: Example Coastal Insurance" kept as context.

error_analysis.title: Date ranges with a separator the parser doesn't accept are not read
error_analysis.observation: The extracted header has a character between the two dates that the date pattern doesn't accept, so the role's months aren't counted.

examples.what: role 'Senior Front-End Engineer, Sample Retail Group': The role was found, but its dates couldn't be read. Between the file and the extracted text, '–' became '·'. Extracted line: "Senior Front-End Engineer at Sample Retail Group, Mar 2022 · Present".

role 'Front-End Developer, Demo Media': The role was found, but its dates couldn't be read. Between the file and the extracted text, '–' became '·'. Extracted line: "Front-End Developer at Demo Media, Jun 2019 · Feb 2022".

role 'Web Developer Intern, Example Agency': The role was found, but its dates couldn't be read. Between the file and the extracted text, '–' became '·'. Extracted line: "Web Developer Intern at Example Agency, Jan 2019 · May 2019".

error_analysis.title: PDF extraction joins a line to the one before it
error_analysis.observation: A line that follows a full-width line, or any line on a page with only short lines, is joined to the previous paragraph, so a role header or an education entry disappears into another line.

examples.what: role 'Software Engineer, Demo Tech Solutions': The header was joined with a neighbouring line during extraction. Extracted line: "Environment: Guidewire BillingCenter 9, CustomerEngage, Gosu, Angular, SQL Server, Bitbucket, Jira Software...".

education 'B.Tech Electronics': The entry was joined with a neighbouring line during extraction. Extracted line: "M.S. Information Technology, Example University, 2013 B.Tech Electronics, Sample Institute of Technology, 2011".

education 'M.S. Information Technology': Read the year 2011, labeled 2013. Extracted line: "M.S. Information Technology, Example University, 2013 B.Tech Electronics, Sample Institute of Technology, 2011".

error_analysis.title: A related skill or a missing detail is counted as direct proof
error_analysis.observation: The catalog files some tools under a broader skill (GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket are terms for Git, JUnit for Unit testing), so a requirement for one tool can be proven by a line that names another. A version the requirement asks for isn't checked either.

examples.what: "Experience with Angular 12 or later": labeled partial, app direct from the experience line "Customized CustomerEngage Angular screens for policy servicing and online payments." (Angular via 'Angular').

"You should be comfortable writing unit tests with Jest or a similar framework.": labeled adjacent, app direct from the experience line "Wrote JUnit tests for the endpoint and fixed 12 bugs from the team backlog." (Unit testing via 'JUnit').

"Experience with Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions": labeled adjacent, app direct from the experience line "Environment: Guidewire PolicyCenter 10, Guidewire Cloud, Gosu, PCF, SOAP, REST, Jenkins..." (Git via 'Git').

error_analysis.title: Roles are found but the title or employer is split wrongly
error_analysis.observation: The role and its dates are read, but extra text stays in the employer (a city and state) or the employer stays in the title, so the role doesn't match its label.

examples.what: role 'Senior Guidewire Developer, Example Mutual': Read as a role with title 'Senior Guidewire Developer' and employer 'Example Mutual, Jacksonville, FL'. Extracted line: "Senior Guidewire Developer, Example Mutual, Jacksonville, FL | Apr 2022 - Till date".

role 'Associate Developer, Sample Software Co': Read as a role with title 'Sample Software Co: Associate Developer' and employer None. Extracted line: "Sample Software Co: Associate Developer, Jun 2016 - Aug 2017".

error_analysis.title: Role header lines in some layouts are read as body text
error_analysis.observation: The line holds a date range the app can read, but it isn't taken as a role header, so the role and its months are lost.

examples.what: role 'Senior Software Engineer, Demo Logistics': The line was kept as body text, not read as a role. It starts with words followed by a colon. Extracted line: "Demo Logistics: Senior Software Engineer, May 2021 - present".

role 'Java Developer, Example Mutual': The line was kept as body text, not read as a role. It starts with words followed by a colon. Extracted line: "Example Mutual: Java Developer, Sep 2017 - Apr 2021".

error_analysis.title: Unknown section headings are kept as requirements
error_analysis.observation: A heading the parser doesn't recognize ("What we need:", "What we offer") is kept as a requirement line, and the lines under it keep the previous section's priority.

examples.what: "What we offer" kept as preferred.
"What we need:" kept as context.

error_analysis.title: Faithful rewrites rejected by the fact checker
error_analysis.observation: The checker errs toward rejecting. A leadership word ("led" for "ran") counts as a bigger claim, and another catalog name for the same skill ("Kubernetes" for "K8s") counts as a new product name.

examples.what: "Moved nightly batch workers from EC2 instances to K8s CronJobs." became "Moved nightly batch workers from EC2 instances to Kubernetes CronJobs.": labeled faithful, checker rejected ("Kubernetes" looks like the name of an organization or product that isn't in the original line.).

"Mentored 4 developers and ran the team's design review meetings." became "Mentored four developers and led the team's design review meetings.": labeled faithful, checker rejected ("led" claims more responsibility than the original line does.).
